componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Model the vent reaction first to show conservation of matter with atom cubes

componentPlan.focusQuote: All photosynthetic organisms use solar energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (food) and oxygen.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Compare sunlight and chemical systems side by side to highlight shared reactants and distinct energy sources

overview.headline: How sunlight and vent chemistry each fuel life on Earth

keyPoints.point: Most life relies on sunlight because plants make food through photosynthesis.
keyPoints.quote: The majority of life on Earth is based on a food web which revolves around the Sun, as plants use sunlight to make food via photosynthesis.

keyPoints.point: Deep sea microbes produce food using chemical energy without sunlight in vent environments.
keyPoints.quote: organisms instead rely on primary production through a process called chemosynthesis, which runs on chemical energy.

keyPoints.point: Matter cannot be created or destroyed, so reactants must fully become products.
keyPoints.quote: Remind students that the law of conservation of matter states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

keyPoints.point: Vent microbes use hydrogen sulfide with carbon dioxide and oxygen to make food.
keyPoints.quote: One common form of chemosynthesis found at hydrothermal vents uses hydrogen sulfide.

keyTerms.gloss: plants convert carbon dioxide and water into food using sunlight energy
keyTerms.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyTerms.gloss: microbes create food using energy released from chemical reactions
keyTerms.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: organisms that make food from raw materials and energy as producers
keyTerms.quote: Autotroph: Organisms that are able to make their own food from raw materials and energy, also known as producers.

keyTerms.gloss: organisms that consume producers or other consumers for nutrition
keyTerms.quote: Heterotroph: Organisms that consume producers or other consumers, also known as consumers.

keyTerms.gloss: starting substance that changes in a chemical reaction
keyTerms.quote: Reactants: A substance that changes in a chemical reaction.

analysis.pageCoverage: Lesson comparing photosynthesis and chemosynthesis with balanced equations, conservation of matter, deep sea vent microbes, food webs, definitions and data table activity
